problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=u(x-2)+u(x-6),\,g(x)=\operatorname{sec}⁡x,\,h(x)=⌊\frac{x}{2}⌋
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌊x⌋$ is the floor function.

feedback.problem:
Which of the following functions are piecewise continuous on $x\in [0,\infty ).$

$$
f(x)=\operatorname{csc}⁡x,\,g(x)=⌊\frac{x}{3}⌋,\,h(x)={\begin{aligned}1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is even} \\ -1,\, & ⌈x⌉\text{ is odd}\end{aligned}
$$

Note that $u(x)$ is the unit step function, and $⌈x⌉$ is the ceiling function.
feedback.worked_solution:
Suppose $I⊆R.$ A function $f:I\to R$ is piecewise continuous on $I$ if it is piecewise continuous on every closed and bounded subinterval $[a,b]⊂I.$

With that in mind, let's examine each function.

- The function $f(x)$ is not piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ Consider the closed subinterval $x\in [0,2\pi ].$ Notice that the one-sided limits at $x=\pi $ are infinite: 

$$
{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{-}}f(x)=+\infty ,\,{lim}_{x\to {\pi }^{+}}f(x)=-\infty .
$$

- The function $g(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=…,-6,-3,0,3,6,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[0,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/370ce6bc297340f28b1e5bcd4a7e0ca3ce5de6edac660e143ac70ba615184765.png)

- The function $h(x)$ is piecewise continuous over $x\in [0,\infty ).$ The function has jump discontinuities at $x=0,1,2,…,$ and any closed interval $[a,b]⊂[0,\infty )$ will contain finitely many discontinuities.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14042449/assets/9b7758701595db784d2d9aeb59cc823316501748976ccbed41980fa29ad0a892.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "$g$ and $h$ only."
